c-rp-change.label: Ratios after something is added
c-rp-change.summary: Write the old quantities as ratio × k (the unknown multiplier), apply the change, and match the new ratio.

c-rp-equal.label: Several quantities tied by percentages
c-rp-equal.summary: 40% of P = 0.5 of Q = 1/8 of R: set them all equal to one number k and read off the ratio.

q-rp-add.label: Ratio changes after adding
q-rp-add.summary: Quantities in a ratio; some are added and the ratio changes; find a number added or the original total.

q-rp-swap.label: Numbers and prices swapped
q-rp-swap.summary: A price ratio and a bill that changes by a % when the quantities are interchanged.

q-rp-chain.label: P : Q : R from percentage links
q-rp-chain.summary: Percentages or fractions of three quantities are equal; find their ratio.

formulas.text: Quantities a : b : c = ak : bk : ck. After adding x to one quantity, form the new ratio and cross-multiply.
formulas.note: One equation in k, then the rest follows.

formulas.text: If a : b becomes c : d after adding, then (ak + p)/(bk + q) = c/d
formulas.note: Use the pair whose added amounts are known first.

formulas.text: If x% of P = y% of Q = z% of R = k, then P : Q : R = 1/x : 1/y : 1/z

q-rp-add.cue: 'Ratio … becomes … after 18 are added' or 'joined by 15 more'.
q-rp-add.standard: Pens 2k : 5k : 7k. Yellow and red give (2k + 18)/(5k + 12) = 3/6 = 1/2, so 4k + 36 = 5k + 12, k = 24. New blue = 8 × (2k + 18)/3 = 176, so 176 − 168 = 8 were added.
q-rp-add.fast: Pick the two quantities whose additions are both known and solve k from them alone; do the third afterwards.
q-rp-add.eliminate: Test options in the final equation: blue 7k + x must be a multiple of 8 in the new ratio. With k = 24, 168 + x ≡ 0 (mod 8), so x is a multiple of 8.
traps: Adding to the ratio numbers instead of to the real quantities (k × ratio).
Using the wrong pair and losing the unknown.
Taking the new ratio as the old one plus the additions.

q-rp-swap.cue: Two kinds of items with a price ratio; the numbers are interchanged and the bill rises by some %.
q-rp-swap.standard: Let a standard machine cost 1 and a premium 6. Original bill 15×6 + n = 90 + n. Swapped bill n×6 + 15 = 1.625(90 + n). So 6n + 15 = 146.25 + 1.625n and n = 30. Ratio 15 : 30 = 1 : 2.
q-rp-swap.fast: Try the option ratios: 1 : 2 means n = 30, original 120, swapped 195, and 195 ÷ 120 = 1.625. ✓
q-rp-swap.eliminate: The bill goes up, so premium machines were fewer than standard ones originally: the ratio is below 1 : 1. All options are, so test them one by one starting with the simplest.
traps: Using 62.5% as 6.25 or 0.625 in the equation.
Forgetting to swap the 15 as well.

q-rp-chain.cue: '40% of P = 0.5 of Q = 1/8 of R. Find P : Q : R.'
q-rp-chain.standard: Let each equal k. P = k/0.4 = 2.5k, Q = k/0.5 = 2k, R = 8k. Ratio 2.5 : 2 : 8 = 5 : 4 : 16.
q-rp-chain.eliminate: 40% is less than 50%, so P must be bigger than Q. Every option with the first term smaller than the second (4 : 5 : 16, 2 : 5 : 8, 4 : 5 : 8) is out at once.
traps: Taking P : Q : R = 40 : 50 : 12.5, i.e. the percentages themselves, instead of their reciprocals.
Mixing percent with fractions without converting (0.5 versus 50).

pyqs.text: A firm ordered 15 premium machines and some standard machines. A premium machine costs 6 times a standard one. By mistake the numbers of premium and standard machines were interchanged, which raised the bill by 62.5%. Find the ratio of premium to standard machines originally ordered.
solution: Let a standard machine cost 1 and a premium 6, and let there be n standard machines. Original bill = 15 × 6 + n = 90 + n.
pyqs.trick: Test 1 : 2: n = 30, original bill 120, swapped bill 195, and 195 ÷ 120 = 1.625.

pyqs.text: The numbers of yellow, red and blue pens in a box are in the ratio 2 : 5 : 7. 18 yellow, 12 red and some blue pens are added, and the ratio becomes 3 : 6 : 8. How many blue pens were added?
solution: Pens are 2k, 5k, 7k. Yellow and red give (2k + 18)/(5k + 12) = 3/6 = 1/2.
New yellow = 66 = 3 parts, so a part is 22 and new blue = 8 × 22 = 176.
pyqs.trick: Use only yellow and red to get k = 24 first; blue then falls out as 176 − 168.

pyqs.text: The ratio of male to female employees in a company is 8 : 6. When 15 more female employees join, the ratio becomes 8 : 7. Find the original total number of employees.
pyqs.trick: Males do not change, so 8 parts stay put: 7 new parts of female = 6 parts + 15, so one part is 15. Total 14 × 15.

c.note: Does not match the worked answer, which is option (b) 210.

a.note: The total must be 14 × 15 = 210; 180 is not a multiple of 14.

d.note: The total of 14 parts must be divisible by 14; 315 is 22.5 parts.

pyqs.text: If 40% of P = 0.5 of Q = 1/8 of R, find P : Q : R.
solution: Let all three equal k. P = k ÷ 0.4 = 2.5k, Q = k ÷ 0.5 = 2k, R = 8k.
pyqs.trick: Take k = 4 so everything is whole: P = 10, Q = 8, R = 32.
